scr_budget_gl_comparison.purpose: Runs the monthly budget-versus-actual (BVA) income statement for a property — actual MTD and YTD against the approved budget by GL line, with dollar and percentage variances — as the basis for the variance commentary the site team and accounting must write for the owner.
scr_budget_gl_comparison.outcome: A variance report showing which revenue and expense lines breached the owner's thresholds (commonly ±$5K and ±10% monthly), driving the variance explanations in the owner package.
scr_budget_gl_comparison.rootCause: The approved budget is the owner's operating plan and often the basis of the property manager's incentive fee. Asset managers must explain NOI performance to investors and lenders, and most management agreements require written variance explanations above set thresholds. The BVA also catches mis-codings: a huge variance on one line and an offsetting one on another usually means an invoice hit the wrong account.
scr_budget_gl_comparison.ifSkipped: Coding errors reach the owner package, the site team cannot explain NOI misses, the asset manager escalates to the management company, and year-end reforecasts are built on bad information.
gaap: Management agreement reporting covenants (budget variance explanations)
Owner/JV operating agreement approval rights over the annual budget
redFlags: Variances explained as 'timing' month after month without a reversal
Variance caused by a mis-coded invoice rather than real performance
Budget loaded to the wrong periods (annual amount in one month)
Actuals compared against a superseded budget version instead of the approved one

scr_budget_model_creation.purpose: Builds next year's property operating budget as a working budget — seeding from the T12 or current-year forecast, applying rent growth, occupancy, concession and bad-debt assumptions, payroll and contract escalators, tax reassessment and insurance renewal estimates — before it is reviewed and approved by the owner.
scr_budget_model_creation.outcome: A complete, account-level monthly operating budget ready for regional and asset-manager review, which will become the approved budget used for BVA reporting and spend controls.
scr_budget_model_creation.rootCause: Owners and JV partners approve an annual budget each fall; it drives distributions, debt covenant forecasts (DSCR), incentive fees and capital planning. A structured budget model makes assumptions explicit and repeatable instead of an untraceable spreadsheet.
scr_budget_model_creation.ifSkipped: The property enters the year with no approved plan, BVA reporting has nothing to compare against, spend controls cannot operate, and the management company may be in breach of its management agreement's budget-delivery deadline.
gaap: Management agreement budget-delivery covenant (typically 60-90 days before fiscal year-end)
Loan documents — lender budget submission for agency loans
reports: Budget vs prior-year and T12 comparison
redFlags: Real estate taxes budgeted flat despite a known reassessment
Management fee not recalculated on budgeted revenue
Monthly seasonality missing (utilities, turnover) — annual amount spread evenly
Rent growth assumptions inconsistent with the revenue management forecast

scr_budget_reforecast_revisions.purpose: Duplicates the approved budget into a new version to produce a mid-year reforecast (6+6 or 9+3: actuals for completed months plus revised projections for the rest) or a formal revision, without overwriting the original approved budget.
scr_budget_reforecast_revisions.outcome: A current full-year outlook that asset managers use for investor updates, distribution planning and covenant forecasts, while the original budget stays intact for accountability.
scr_budget_reforecast_revisions.rootCause: Market conditions change during the year (rent growth, insurance spikes, tax appeals). Owners need an updated forecast, but performance must still be measured against the original approved budget. Separate versions allow both.
scr_budget_reforecast_revisions.ifSkipped: Either the original budget is overwritten (destroying the accountability baseline and incentive-fee calculations) or investors receive stale forecasts, leading to surprise covenant breaches or distribution shortfalls.
gaap: JV/fund reporting — quarterly forecast updates to investors
redFlags: Original budget version modified instead of duplicated

scr_budget_variance_threshold_locking.purpose: Configures budget checks on approvals so that an A/P invoice or purchase order that would push a GL line over its approved budget either warns the approver or is blocked outright until someone with authority overrides it.
scr_budget_variance_threshold_locking.outcome: Over-budget spend is stopped or escalated before the obligation is incurred rather than discovered after the month closes.
scr_budget_variance_threshold_locking.rootCause: Owners delegate spending authority to management companies within an approved budget; management agreements typically require owner approval for unbudgeted spend over a threshold (e.g., $5K-$25K). A preventive system control is stronger than after-the-fact variance explanations.
scr_budget_variance_threshold_locking.ifSkipped: Unbudgeted spend is only discovered in BVA reporting, the management company breaches its delegated authority, and owners may refuse to fund or reimburse the expense.
redFlags: Budget checks set to 'warn' on lines the owner requires hard stops for
Overrides granted by the same person who requested the spend
Budget checks running against a draft instead of the approved budget
